newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: INSTANT VIEW - PORTUGAL CPI UNCHANGED IN JULY.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - PORTUGAL CPI UNCHANGED IN JULY.

text.p: Following are some reactions from analysts to news that Portugal's consumer price index (CPI) was unchanged in July compared with June. The 1.7 percent year-on-year rise was at the better end of analysts' forecasts.

"This CPI makes the government's target (of an average rate of 2.25-2.50 percent for this year) more attainable. Depending on what happens over the next couple of months, the (12-month rolling average) rate could even be between 2.1 and 2.2 percent. The Bank of Portugal has room to cut rates but I don't know whether it will be this month. It depends on the currency market."
JORGE FERRAZ, IMF-Informacao de Mercados Financeiros:

"It is a good number but I fear a little artificial because it reflects the end of the (statistical) influence of the "mad cow" disease scare. It is a number that appears to be running against the trend in other countries, particularly Germany. I think that the Bank of Portugal will take a cool look at the number and will wait for next month. I don't think (next month) will be such a pleasant figure because we are beginning to suffer some imported inflation. I don't think that the Bank of Portugal has room to cut rates this month because of the performance of the currency market."
PEDRO BRAZ TEIXEIRA, BANCO SANTANDER DE NEGOCIOS PORTUGAL:

"At a glance, the food sector would be responsible for the favourable performance of inflation. This 2.7 percent (12-month rolling average) means...that Portugal will fulfill the Maastricht (inflation) criteria and with increasing ease."

"It was a very good number, a bit better than we had been predicting, but I think that in terms of market (interest) rates, it is not going to have a big impact. There is still concern about a possible (repo) rate rise in Germany. There was already the expectation that the Bank of Portugal would not touch rates again that soon, and it will probably wait around another month...until this concern disappears that the Bundesbank will raise the repo to defend the mark."

"It is a good number, even if inside the expectations, with the decline in the food sector the reason. It gives the Bank of Portugal some room to cut rates, but I think it will not happen next week due to the easing of the escudo on the foreign exchanges. But it opens room for (future) rate cuts because our year-on-year rate is 0.1 of a percent below Spain, and there is still a wide difference in the repo rates.
(The repo rate in Spain stands at 5.25 percent against 5.70 percent in Portugal).
